svg.aria-label: Four shapes a field takes in real markup: the name in one attribute and the value in another, the tag itself as the name, the class or id as the name, and the name carried inside the value. A fifth is the same shape as the fourth and wrong, because the element had a real name source that was read past.
svg.text: what survives translation is the tag and the standardised attribute, not the class
A · the name is one attribute, the value another
meta -> property -> contains("title") -> @content
8 to 10 of 13 domains. Language independent by
specification: og: is English on Russian pages.
B · the tag is the name
time -> <tag> -> means("date") -> @datetime
h1 on 13 of 13, time[datetime] on 10 of 13. The only
shape that works when every class is Tailwind.
C · the class or id is the name
h1 -> class -> contains("title") -> text()
entry-title, news__title, single-news-title. Not
language independent: what about class="titulo"?
D · the name is inside the value
img -> alt -> splitLabel() -> "Author" : "THE NEWSROOM"
The same form as "Make: Toyota". The string carries
its own label, so one slot is both name and value.
E · the same structure as D, and wrong
link -> title -> "West Florida News" won title on 19 of 19 sites
link -> href -> "https://i0.wp.com" won link on 19 of 19 sites
The element had a real name source and inference read past it: rel="alternate", rel="preconnect".
D and E have the same structure and opposite verdicts. That is the thing to resolve.
Every line here is taken from the crawled corpus rather than invented, which is why the shapes are
awkward: an attribute literally named title is not the title, and canonical is on 10 of 13 sites unused.
